title: Palisades (Holtec restart): External_Sender Palisades Fuel Damage LAR Public Comment [['E-Mail', 'Letter']]

documents.text:
From:          Arnie Gundersen
To:            Marlayna Doell
Subject:       [External_Sender] Palisades Fuel Damage LAR Public Comment
Date:          Wednesday, October 7, 2026 10:35:09 PM
Attachments:   IMG_5936.PNG




Dear Protectors of the Public’s Health and Safety at the NRC,

WHY ARE YOU IN SUCH A RUSH TO HELP HOLTEC RESURRECT
PALISADES????

As a formerly licensed AEC Reactor Operator, I view safely loading any nuclear
reactor core as a sacred duty the public entrusted me with. The repeated "one-over-
M" calculations to avoid inadvertent criticality that are required as fuel is loaded
have been deeply impressed into my soul.

Fuel Loading should not be trivialized as a marketing photo op, yet that is exactly
what Holtec did at Palisades by filming the first eight fuel elements loaded into the
Palisades core and bragging about it on their Facebook page on August 31, 2026.
  

      : The official Palisades Energy Facebook Page posted the specific image
      capturing the milestone of the first eight nuclear fuel bundles entering
      the reactor vessel. * Facebook • Holtec Palisades


Yet as soon as Holtec turned the cameras off, they managed to drop one of the next
fuel bundles. According to Reddit, Holtec’s own employees have viewed photos
of the dropped fuel bundle and believe it is a “BIG uh-oh” and “the worst fuel
handling fuck up I’ve ever seen… its ugly”. (See below)

That Holtec widely disseminated video of its first eight successful bundle insertions
trivializes the safety significance and shows a the lack of a safety conscious work
environment at Palisades. Trivializing fuel load show the lack of appreciation for
its safety significance and is likely the root cause of the bundle drop. Neither the
NRC nor Holtec acknowledged that failure until three weeks later when the press
had already identified it from Holtec’s employee concerns posted on Reddit. And
the photos of the bundle are still not provided to the public.

What is your rush to restart Palisades by a rookie owner, Holtec??? AT LEAST
THREE ISSUES NEED TO BE ADDRESSED:
1. There is absolutely nothing on the record to explain the root cause of why and
 how the fuel bundle was dropped and how such an event will be avoided in the
future.
2. Nor is there anything on the record to analyze what damage might have been
caused when the fuel bundle fell.
3. A safety conscious workplace needs to be created, not a photo op culture.

Running a nuclear power plant should not be a photo op! I understand that both the
NRC staff and Holtec staff are under pressure for their respective managements to
quickly resurrect Palisades, but maintaining an adequate safety culture is not open
for negotiation.

Arnie Gundersen
AEC Reactor License #OP-3014
 Sent from my iPhone
